name: Optic disc edema
definition: Swelling of the optic nerve head from axoplasmic stasis, seen as an elevated, hyperaemic disc with blurred margins and obscuration of vessels at the disc edge, of any cause (e.g. NAION, optic neuritis/papillitis, raised intracranial pressure).

location.notes: Disc and immediately adjacent peripapillary nerve fibre layer; may be sectoral (e.g. altitudinal in NAION).

typical_size: Whole disc (1 DD) plus a 0.25-0.5 DD peripapillary halo

drawing.description: Fill the disc circle yellow and feather its margin with short radial yellow strokes into the peripapillary retina to show blurred margins; add peripapillary flame haemorrhages as red strokes if present.

color_source: inferred: CMS L33567 App A yellow = intraretinal edema; no standard disc-swelling code exists (Jayanna S, Shanmugam PM. It is time for more colors! Indian J Ophthalmol 2022, https://doi.org/10.4103/ijo.IJO_1004_22)

pubmed.title: Resolution of disc oedema in nonarteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy versus optic neuritis: a retrospective, cross-sectional study.
Optical Coherence Tomography Neuro-Toolbox for the Diagnosis and Management of Papilledema, Optic Disc Edema, and Pseudopapilledema.

name: Papilledema
definition: Optic disc swelling secondary to raised intracranial pressure, usually bilateral, with visual function typically preserved in the acute phase.

location.notes: Both discs; may be accompanied by peripapillary haemorrhages, cotton-wool spots and peripapillary retinal/choroidal folds.

typical_size: Whole disc plus peripapillary halo, up to about 1 DD beyond the margin in severe cases

drawing.description: Draw on both eye charts: fill each disc yellow with feathered radial yellow margins; add red flame haemorrhages and yellow cotton-wool spots around the disc where seen.

color_source: inferred: CMS L33567 App A yellow = intraretinal edema; red = retinal hemorrhages

pubmed.title: Papilledema: A review of etiology, pathophysiology, diagnosis, and management.
Anemia and papilledema.

name: Optic disc pallor / optic atrophy
definition: Loss of the normal pink colour of the neuroretinal rim from loss of retinal ganglion cell axons, diffuse or sectoral (e.g. temporal pallor from papillomacular bundle loss).

location.notes: Whole disc or a sector of the rim; temporal sector in papillomacular bundle disease.

typical_size: Whole disc or a sector of it (1 DD)

drawing.description: Outline the disc in black and leave the pale area white, shading only the affected sector for sectoral pallor; annotate the sector (e.g. 'temporal pallor').

color_source: inferred: natural-colour depiction; no standard code exists for disc pallor (Jayanna S, Shanmugam PM. Indian J Ophthalmol 2022, https://doi.org/10.4103/ijo.IJO_1004_22)

pubmed.title: Pediatric Optic Disc Pallor.
Dominant optic atrophy: updates on the pathophysiology and clinical manifestations of the optic atrophy 1 mutation.

name: Glaucomatous optic disc cupping
definition: Enlargement and deepening of the optic cup with diffuse or focal thinning (notching) of the neuroretinal rim from glaucomatous axon loss, often with vertical elongation of the cup.

location.typical_clock: superior and inferior poles of the disc
location.notes: Rim loss characteristically at the inferotemporal and superotemporal poles; record the vertical cup-to-disc ratio.

typical_size: Recorded as vertical cup-to-disc ratio (e.g. 0.7) within a 1 DD disc

drawing.description: Draw a second black oval inside the disc circle to mark the cup margin, sized to the vertical C/D ratio; show focal notches as indentations of the rim and write the ratio beside the disc.

color_source: inferred: black outline for a structural landmark; CMS L33567 App A only asks that optic nerve 'cupping' be recorded, without a colour

pubmed.title: Diagnosis and pathogenesis of glaucomatous optic neuropathy: morphological aspects.

name: Optic disc hemorrhage (Drance)
definition: Splinter- or flame-shaped haemorrhage on or crossing the optic disc margin, a recognised marker of glaucomatous damage and progression.

location.notes: Straddles the disc rim into the peripapillary nerve fibre layer, oriented radially.

typical_size: 0.1-0.25 DD in length

drawing.description: Draw a short radial red stroke crossing the disc margin at the involved clock hour.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

pubmed.title: Optic disc hemorrhage in glaucoma: pathophysiology and prognostic significance.
Diagnosis and pathogenesis of glaucomatous optic neuropathy: morphological aspects.

name: Optic disc pit
definition: Rare congenital circumscribed greyish depression in the optic disc, usually temporal, that may lead to macular schisis and serous macular detachment.

location.notes: Within the disc margin; associated macular fluid extends from the disc toward the fovea.

typical_size: About 1/8-1/3 DD

drawing.description: Draw a small black-outlined oval at the temporal disc stippled black to show the grey pit; draw any associated serous macular detachment in blue.

color_source: inferred: grey depression shown as black stipple; associated detachment blue per CMS L33567 App A

pubmed.title: Optic disc pit: a review.
Optic disc pit maculopathy: a review of diagnosis and treatment.

name: Optic disc coloboma
definition: Congenital excavation of the optic disc from incomplete closure of the embryonic fissure, seen as an enlarged, sharply demarcated, white bowl-shaped defect that is deeper inferiorly.

location.notes: Excavation decentred inferiorly; may be continuous with an inferior chorioretinal coloboma.

typical_size: Enlarged disc, larger than 1 DD

drawing.description: Enlarge the disc circle inferiorly with a black outline and leave the excavation white; draw any contiguous chorioretinal coloboma with the same code.

color_source: inferred: white bare excavation with black margin; optic disc anomalies have no standard code (Jayanna S, Shanmugam PM. Indian J Ophthalmol 2022, https://doi.org/10.4103/ijo.IJO_1004_22)

pubmed.title: Congenital Optic Disc Anomalies: Insights from Multimodal Imaging.
Retinal complications associated with congenital optic disc anomalies determined by swept source optical coherence tomography.

name: Morning glory disc anomaly
definition: Congenital funnel-shaped excavation of an enlarged optic disc with a central white glial tuft, a surrounding ring of chorioretinal pigmentary change, and numerous straight vessels radiating from the disc margin.

location.notes: Disc plus a peripapillary ring of pigmentary disturbance; usually unilateral.

typical_size: Enlarged disc with peripapillary ring, larger than 1 DD

drawing.description: Draw an enlarged disc with a white centre (glial tuft), a black-stippled peripapillary pigment ring, and many straight red vessels radiating from its edge.

color_source: inferred: white glial tissue; black = pigment (Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044); red vessels per CMS L33567 App A

pubmed.title: Update on the morning glory disc anomaly.
Retinal complications associated with congenital optic disc anomalies determined by swept source optical coherence tomography.

name: Optic disc drusen
definition: Acellular, often calcified deposits in the prelaminar optic nerve head, visible as refractile yellow-white lumpy bodies when superficial or causing an elevated disc that mimics papilledema when buried.

location.notes: Within the disc substance, giving a lumpy or scalloped margin; frequently bilateral.

typical_size: Small nodules within a 1 DD disc

drawing.description: Draw clusters of small yellow circles within the disc circle and give the disc a lumpy, scalloped margin.

color_source: inferred: drusen are stippled yellow (Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology, https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology)

pubmed.title: Optic disc drusen: a systematic review : Up-to-date and future perspective.
Prevalence of optic disc drusen: A systematic review, meta-analysis and forecasting study.

name: Myelinated retinal nerve fibres
definition: Congenital patch of myelinated retinal nerve fibre layer appearing as a white, opaque, feathery-edged patch that follows the nerve fibre pattern and obscures the underlying retinal vessels.

location.notes: Usually contiguous with the disc margin along the arcuate bundles; occasionally an isolated patch elsewhere.

typical_size: 0.5 DD to several DD

drawing.description: Shade a white patch following the arcuate nerve fibre direction, with fine black feathered strokes at its frayed edges; draw vessels within it as interrupted.

color_source: inferred: natural white colour; no standard code

pubmed.title: Myelinated Retinal Nerve Fiber Layer (RNFL): A Comprehensive Review.

name: Peripapillary (parapapillary) atrophy
definition: Crescent or ring of chorioretinal atrophy adjacent to the optic disc; the beta zone exposes sclera and large choroidal vessels next to the disc margin, and the alpha zone shows irregular hypo/hyperpigmentation outside it.

location.notes: Crescent abutting the disc margin; may encircle the disc in high myopia or glaucoma.

typical_size: Crescent 0.1-1 DD wide

drawing.description: Draw a crescent against the (usually temporal) disc margin bounded by a black line: leave the inner beta zone white and stipple the outer alpha zone black for irregular pigment.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (BLACK = RPE, pigment clumping); white bare sclera inferred

pubmed.title: Beta-Zone parapapillary atrophy and the velocity of glaucoma progression.
Controversies in the association of parapapillary atrophy with glaucoma.

name: Tilted disc
definition: Congenital oblique insertion of the optic nerve producing an oval, obliquely oriented disc with an inferonasal crescent, situs inversus of the retinal vessels and inferonasal RPE/choroidal hypoplasia.

location.notes: Oval disc with oblique long axis; crescent and ectatic hypopigmented fundus inferonasally.

typical_size: Disc plus inferonasal crescent

drawing.description: Draw the disc as an oblique oval with a white, black-outlined crescent at its inferonasal edge; lightly mark any inferonasal ectatic zone.

color_source: inferred: white bare-sclera crescent with black margin

pubmed.title: Tilted disc syndrome.
Macular associations of tilted disc syndrome.

name: Optic nerve hypoplasia
definition: Congenitally small optic disc with reduced axon number, characteristically surrounded by a peripapillary double-ring sign, often with tortuous retinal vessels and nerve fibre layer thinning.

location.notes: Small disc within a larger scleral-canal ring; unilateral or bilateral.

typical_size: Disc clearly smaller than 1 normal DD

drawing.description: Draw a reduced disc circle with a second concentric black ring around it to show the double-ring sign.

color_source: inferred: black outline for structural landmark

pubmed.title: Optic nerve hypoplasia.

name: Optic disc melanocytoma
definition: Benign, deeply pigmented magnocellular nevus of the optic disc, dark brown to black, often eccentric on the disc and frequently extending into the adjacent choroid or retina.

location.notes: On the disc, often eccentric, overhanging the margin when it has a choroidal (54%) or retinal (30%) component; 99% unilateral.

typical_size: Mean about 2 mm diameter (about 1.3 DD) and 1 mm thick

drawing.description: Fill the involved part of the disc solid dark brown with a black outline, extending past the margin where there is a choroidal or retinal component.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (BROWN = melanocytic lesions)

pubmed.title: Melanocytoma of optic disc in 115 cases: the 2004 Samuel Johnson Memorial Lecture, part 1.

name: Choroidal nevus
definition: Benign, well-circumscribed, flat or minimally elevated slate-grey to brown melanocytic choroidal lesion, often with overlying drusen; risk features include thickness >2 mm, subretinal fluid, orange pigment and margin <3 mm from the disc.

location.notes: Mostly postequatorial but can occur anywhere in the choroid.

typical_size: Mean basal diameter about 1.25 mm (about 1 DD) in population studies; giant nevus 10 mm or more; thickness up to 2 mm

drawing.description: Fill a flat round or oval patch solid brown; add overlying drusen as yellow dots and any subretinal fluid in blue.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

pubmed.title: Choroidal nevus: a review of prevalence, features, genetics, risks, and outcomes.
Estimating the risk of malignant transformation of a choroidal nevus.

name: Choroidal melanoma
definition: Malignant melanocytic tumour of the choroid presenting as an elevated brown dome- or mushroom (collar-button)-shaped mass, often with orange pigment and associated subretinal fluid.

location.notes: Anywhere in the choroid, may extend anteriorly into the ciliary body; frequently with exudative retinal detachment.

typical_size: Thickness: small 0-3 mm, medium 3.1-8 mm, large >8 mm; basal diameter usually several DD

drawing.description: Draw a solid brown dome; for a collar-button tumour draw a narrowed waist where it breaks through Bruch membrane; draw associated serous detachment in blue.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology, https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (BROWN = malignant choroidal melanomas)

pubmed.title: Metastasis of uveal melanoma millimeter-by-millimeter in 8033 consecutive eyes.
Using risk factors for detection and prognostication of uveal melanoma.
[Collar-button choroidal melanoma. Anatomo-radiologic correlations].

name: Amelanotic choroidal melanoma
definition: Choroidal melanoma with little or no pigment, appearing as a yellow-tan to pinkish elevated dome or mushroom mass, often with visible intrinsic vessels.

location.notes: Anywhere in the choroid; differential includes metastasis and hemangioma.

typical_size: As for pigmented melanoma (small 0-3 mm, medium 3.1-8 mm, large >8 mm thick)

drawing.description: Fill the dome yellow (amelanotic mass) with a brown outline to mark it as a choroidal tumour; draw subretinal fluid in blue.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (YELLOW = amelanotic mass lesions); brown outline = choroidal tumour (Requisites for fundus drawing, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retina-drwaing/163697941)

pubmed.title: Amelanotic choroidal melanoma.
Metastasis of uveal melanoma millimeter-by-millimeter in 8033 consecutive eyes.

name: Circumscribed choroidal hemangioma
definition: Benign solitary vascular hamartoma of the choroid presenting as a smooth, orange-red, elevated mass posterior to the equator, frequently with subretinal fluid or cystoid macular edema.

location.notes: Posterior to the equator, commonly macular or juxtapapillary; unilateral and solitary.

typical_size: Usually several DD in basal diameter, a few mm thick

drawing.description: Draw a red-filled dome with a brown outline marking its choroidal origin; add overlying serous detachment in blue.

color_source: Jayanna S, Shanmugam PM. It is time for more colors! Indian J Ophthalmol 2022, https://doi.org/10.4103/ijo.IJO_1004_22 (choroidal vascular tumours such as hemangioma coded red); brown outline = choroidal tumour (https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology)

pubmed.title: Circumscribed Choroidal Hemangioma.
Circumscribed choroidal hemangioma.

name: Diffuse choroidal hemangioma
definition: Diffuse vascular hamartomatous thickening of the choroid, characteristic of Sturge-Weber syndrome, giving a deep red-orange fundus colour and often complicated by exudative retinal detachment.

location.notes: Diffuse, ill-defined, involving much of the posterior choroid of one eye (side of the facial port-wine stain).

typical_size: Extensive, often more than one quadrant

drawing.description: Shade the involved fundus red with an ill-defined brown border; draw any exudative detachment in blue.

color_source: Jayanna S, Shanmugam PM. Indian J Ophthalmol 2022, https://doi.org/10.4103/ijo.IJO_1004_22 (choroidal vascular tumours coded red); brown = choroidal tumour (https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology)

pubmed.title: Current concepts on diffuse choroidal hemangioma in Sturge Weber syndrome.

name: Choroidal metastasis
definition: Secondary choroidal tumour, most often from breast or lung carcinoma, appearing as a creamy yellow plateau-shaped mass with subretinal fluid, frequently multifocal or bilateral.

location.notes: Epicentre between macula and equator in 80%, macula 12%, anterior to equator 8%; mean two tumours per eye.

typical_size: Mean basal diameter about 9 mm (about 6 DD), about 3 mm thick

drawing.description: Draw each focus as a flat-topped yellow mass with a brown outline; draw the associated subretinal fluid in blue.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (YELLOW = amelanotic mass lesions); brown = choroidal tumours (https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology)

pubmed.title: Survey of 520 eyes with uveal metastases.

name: Choroidal osteoma
definition: Benign ossifying tumour of the choroid, typically in young women, appearing as a yellow-orange, well-demarcated, scalloped, slightly elevated plaque with pigment mottling, often juxtapapillary.

location.notes: Juxtapapillary or macular; clinically unilateral in 75%; choroidal neovascularisation in up to one third.

typical_size: Several DD with geographic scalloped margins

drawing.description: Fill a scalloped-edged plaque yellow with a brown outline and brown stippling for pigment mottling; mark CNV with the CMS neovascularisation colours if present.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (YELLOW = amelanotic mass lesions); brown outline/stipple inferred from CMS L33567 App A brown = choroidal pigmentation

pubmed.title: Choroidal osteoma.
Choroidal osteoma.

name: Congenital hypertrophy of the RPE (solitary)
synonyms: congenital hypertrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium
definition: Congenital, flat, sharply demarcated, uniformly dark RPE lesion with a depigmented halo and frequent depigmented lacunae, usually equatorial or peripheral.

location.notes: Equatorial region in 45%, inferotemporal quadrant most often (31%); rarely macular or peripapillary (1% each).

typical_size: Median largest basal diameter 4.5 mm (about 3 DD)

drawing.description: Fill a flat round patch with scalloped edge solid brown, leave a thin unpainted rim for the depigmented halo, and leave small white holes for lacunae.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

pubmed.title: Solitary congenital hypertrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium: clinical features and frequency of enlargement in 330 patients.

name: Grouped CHRPE (bear tracks)
synonyms: congenital grouped pigmentation of the rpe
grouped congenital hypertrophy of the rpe
definition: Clusters of small, flat, sharply demarcated pigmented RPE lesions arranged sectorally like animal footprints, enlarging from near the disc toward the periphery.

location.notes: Sectoral, radiating from near the disc margin to the periphery, usually confined to one sector or quadrant; smaller spots near the disc, larger peripherally.

typical_size: Spots from a fraction of a DD near the disc to about 1 DD peripherally, occupying a sector

drawing.description: Draw groups of small solid brown blobs in a wedge-shaped sector, enlarging toward the ora.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

pubmed.title: Grouped congenital hypertrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium follows developmental patterns of pigmentary mosaicism.
Diffuse bear-track retina: profound, bilateral, grouped congenital pigmentation of the retinal pigment epithelium in an infant.

name: Congenital grouped albinotic spots (polar bear tracks)
definition: Rare benign congenital groups of flat, well-circumscribed white RPE spots, the non-pigmented counterpart of bear-track pigmentation.

location.notes: Predominantly unilateral, grouped in a sector.

typical_size: Variably sized spots, a fraction of a DD each

drawing.description: Draw grouped small white spots, each thinly outlined in black, in a sectoral cluster.

color_source: inferred: white depigmented spots with black outline for visibility (no standard code)

pubmed.title: Congenital Grouped Albinotic Spots: New Insights on the Pathophysiology Based on Multimodal Retinal Imaging.
Multimodal imaging characteristics of congenital grouped hyper- and hypo-pigmented fundus lesions.

name: FAP-associated pigmented RPE lesions
definition: Multiple (three or more) and/or bilateral CHRPE-like pigmented RPE lesions that serve as an early phenotypic marker of familial adenomatous polyposis.

location.notes: Scattered in both fundi.

typical_size: Small, generally smaller than solitary CHRPE

drawing.description: Draw multiple small brown ovals scattered in both fundi and annotate the count per eye.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

pubmed.title: Congenital Hypertrophy of the Retinal Pigment Epithelium (CHRPE) as a Screening Marker for Familial Adenomatous Polyposis (FAP): Systematic Literature Review and Screening Recommendations.
Fundus lesions of adenomatous polyposis.

name: RPE hyperplasia / pigment clumps
definition: Reactive proliferation and migration of RPE cells producing focal black pigment clumps or plaques, typically at sites of prior inflammation, trauma or detachment, or adjacent to tumours.

location.notes: Wherever the inciting process was; often at scar margins.

typical_size: Pinpoint to about 1 DD

drawing.description: Draw solid black dots or irregular black clumps at the site.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (BLACK = pigment clumping, retinal pigmentation)

pubmed.title: Idiopathic reactive hyperplasia of the retinal pigment epithelium.
Advances in multimodal imaging for diagnosis of pigmented ocular fundus lesions.

name: Combined hamartoma of the retina and RPE
synonyms: combined hamartoma of retina and rpe
combined hamartoma of the retina and retinal pigment epithelium
definition: Benign, slightly elevated, grey-black lesion of disorganised retina, glial tissue, vessels and RPE, with a surface membrane causing retinal traction and vascular tortuosity, usually juxtapapillary or macular.

location.notes: Juxtapapillary 76%, macular 17%, peripheral 7% in a pooled series.

typical_size: About 1 to several DD

drawing.description: Fill the lesion brown for its pigmented component, outline it in green for the epiretinal/glial membrane, and draw the dragged, tortuous vessels as wavy red lines across it.

color_source: inferred: CMS L33567 App A brown = RPE pigmentation; green = preretinal membranes (Jayanna S, Shanmugam PM. Indian J Ophthalmol 2022, https://doi.org/10.4103/ijo.IJO_1004_22); red vessels per CMS

pubmed.title: Combined hamartoma of sensory retina and retinal pigment epithelium.
Peripapillary Versus Macular Combined Hamartoma of the Retina and Retinal Pigment Epithelium: Imaging Characteristics.

name: Retinal astrocytic hamartoma
definition: Benign glial tumour of the retinal nerve fibre layer, cream-white and well-circumscribed, either flat and semitranslucent or elevated, calcified and multilobulated ('mulberry'), associated with tuberous sclerosis.

location.notes: Posterior pole, often near the disc; multiple and bilateral in tuberous sclerosis; may be isolated.

typical_size: Usually up to 1-2 DD

drawing.description: Draw a cream-white nodule filled yellow; for the calcified mulberry type draw small lobules within it.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (YELLOW = amelanotic mass lesions)

pubmed.title: Retinal astrocytic hamartoma.
RETINAL ASTROCYTIC HAMARTOMA: Optical Coherence Tomography Classification and Correlation With Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.

name: Retinal capillary hemangioblastoma
definition: Benign retinal vascular tumour, often the first manifestation of von Hippel-Lindau disease, appearing as a round orange-red mass supplied by a dilated tortuous feeding artery and draining vein, with exudation.

location.notes: Mostly peripheral; juxtapapillary/endophytic variant on or beside the disc; may be multiple and bilateral.

typical_size: Pinpoint to several DD

drawing.description: Draw a round red mass with a dilated red feeder artery and blue draining vein running toward the disc; add yellow exudate and blue exudative detachment if present.

color_source: Jayanna S, Shanmugam PM. It is time for more colors! Indian J Ophthalmol 2022, https://doi.org/10.4103/ijo.IJO_1004_22 (retinal tumours such as angiomas coded red); vessels per CMS L33567 App A

pubmed.title: Retinal Capillary Hemangioblastoma: A Comprehensive Review on Treatments.
A meta-analysis of different von Hippel Lindau mutations: are they related to retinal capillary hemangioblastoma?

name: Retinal cavernous hemangioma
definition: Rare congenital retinal vascular hamartoma made of clustered thin-walled, dark-red saccular aneurysms ('cluster of grapes') with grey-white surface fibrosis, without feeder vessels or exudation.

location.notes: Usually unilateral and unifocal; may lie on the disc or in the retina; intracranial involvement in about 14%.

typical_size: About 1 to several DD

drawing.description: Draw a cluster of small dark-red circles (saccules); outline any overlying grey-white fibroglial tissue in green.

color_source: Jayanna S, Shanmugam PM. Indian J Ophthalmol 2022, https://doi.org/10.4103/ijo.IJO_1004_22 (retinal vascular tumours red; preretinal fibrosis green)

pubmed.title: CAVERNOUS HEMANGIOMA OF THE RETINA: A Comprehensive Review of the Literature (1934-2015).

name: Retinoblastoma
definition: Malignant retinal tumour of infancy and childhood appearing as a white, chalky, often calcified, vascularised retinal mass that grows into the vitreous (endophytic, with seeds) or beneath the retina (exophytic, with detachment); presents with leucocoria.

location.notes: Anywhere in the retina; unifocal or multifocal; bilateral in heritable disease.

typical_size: From under 1 DD to filling the globe

drawing.description: Draw each tumour filled yellow with a blue outline; draw vitreous seeds as green dots and any exudative detachment in blue.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology, https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (retinoblastomas outlined in blue and coloured yellow)

pubmed.title: Retinoblastoma.

name: Vasoproliferative tumour of the retina
definition: Acquired idiopathic or secondary yellow-pink to red retinal vascular mass in the peripheral fundus with minimally dilated feeder vessels, intraretinal exudation and frequent exudative detachment.

location.notes: Inferior, inferotemporal or temporal in 78%; within 6 mm of the ora in 88%; secondary forms follow pars planitis, retinitis pigmentosa, toxoplasmosis, coloboma.

typical_size: About 1 to several DD

drawing.description: Draw a red nodule near the ora; surround it with yellow exudate dots, draw exudative detachment in blue and adjacent RPE hyperplasia in black.

color_source: Jayanna S, Shanmugam PM. Indian J Ophthalmol 2022, https://doi.org/10.4103/ijo.IJO_1004_22 (retinal vascular tumours coded red)

pubmed.title: Vasoproliferative tumors of the ocular fundus. Classification and clinical manifestations in 103 patients.
Retinal vasoproliferative tumors in ocular conditions of childhood.

name: Chorioretinal (choroidal) coloboma
definition: Congenital absence of retina, RPE and choroid along the inferonasal embryonic fissure, seen as a sharply demarcated white area of bare sclera with pigmented margins, covered by a thin intercalary membrane.

location.notes: Inferior to the disc, may include the disc and extend to the periphery; RD (breaks in or outside the coloboma) and CNV at its margin are complications.

typical_size: From about 1 DD to a large sector reaching the ora

drawing.description: Outline the defect in black for its pigmented margin and leave it white; mark any break in the intercalary membrane with the CMS retinal-break code.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (BLACK = pigment); white bare sclera inferred

pubmed.title: Chorioretinal Coloboma Complications: Retinal Detachment and Choroidal Neovascular Membrane.
Chorioretinal coloboma in a paediatric population.
Review of evidence for environmental causes of uveal coloboma.

name: Vitreoretinal lymphoma
definition: Intraocular large B-cell lymphoma that masquerades as uveitis, with vitreous cells/haze and creamy yellow subretinal (sub-RPE) infiltrates.

location.notes: Vitreous plus multifocal posterior subretinal infiltrates; often bilateral.

typical_size: Infiltrates about 0.25 to several DD

drawing.description: Draw subretinal infiltrates as yellow patches and overlay vitreous cells/haze as a green stippled cloud.

color_source: inferred: CMS L33567 App A yellow = chorioretinal exudate; green = opacities in media

pubmed.title: Vitreoretinal Lymphoma: A Literature Review and Introduction of a New Diagnostic Method.
Primary vitreoretinal lymphoma: empowering our clinical suspicion.

name: Toxoplasma retinochoroiditis (active)
definition: Focal necrotising retinochoroiditis caused by Toxoplasma gondii, seen as a fluffy yellow-white retinal lesion, often a satellite at the edge of an old pigmented scar, with overlying vitritis.

location.notes: Frequently posterior pole/macula but may be anywhere; recurrences adjacent to old scars.

typical_size: Usually about 1-3 DD

drawing.description: Fill a fluffy-edged patch yellow beside any black-bordered scar; overlay a green stippled vitreous haze above it.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (YELLOW = retinal inflammation); green vitreous haze per CMS L33567 App A

pubmed.title: Ocular toxoplasmosis: a review of the current diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.
Coexisting choroidal neovascularization and active retinochoroiditis-an uncommon presentation of ocular toxoplasmosis.

name: Toxoplasma retinochoroidal scar (inactive)
definition: Healed toxoplasmic retinochoroiditis: a punched-out atrophic chorioretinal scar with a white bare-sclera centre and hyperpigmented borders, the usual site of satellite recurrences.

location.notes: Macula/posterior pole common; may be multiple.

typical_size: About 0.5 to several DD

drawing.description: Outline the scar in black, leave the centre white, and stipple black pigment along its edge.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (BLACK = scar, pigment clumping); white bare-sclera centre inferred

pubmed.title: Coexisting choroidal neovascularization and active retinochoroiditis-an uncommon presentation of ocular toxoplasmosis.
Ocular Toxoplasmosis: A Review of Current Literature.

name: CMV retinitis
definition: Necrotising retinitis from cytomegalovirus in immunocompromised patients, seen as yellow-white granular retinal necrosis with intraretinal haemorrhage ('pizza pie') or an indolent granular border, with only mild vitritis.

location.notes: Usually starts in the peripheral retina and advances toward the posterior pole, often along vascular arcades.

typical_size: From under 1 DD to several clock hours

drawing.description: Fill the necrotic area yellow with scattered red dots and blots for haemorrhage; give it a granular, stippled advancing border.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (YELLOW = retinal inflammation); red haemorrhages per CMS L33567 App A

pubmed.title: Cytomegalovirus Retinitis: Clinical Manifestations, Diagnosis and Treatment.

name: Acute retinal necrosis
definition: Rapidly progressive necrotising herpetic (VZV/HSV) retinitis, typically in immunocompetent patients, with confluent peripheral yellow-white necrosis, occlusive retinal arteritis and prominent vitritis, frequently complicated by retinal detachment.

location.notes: Begins in the peripheral retina and spreads circumferentially and posteriorly; second eye involved in a proportion of cases.

typical_size: 1 to 12 clock hours

drawing.description: Draw a circumferential yellow band in the periphery with a scalloped posterior edge; add green vitreous haze and, later, breaks/detachment with the CMS codes.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (YELLOW = retinal inflammation)

pubmed.title: Diagnostic and therapeutic challenges in acute retinal necrosis; an update.
Acute retinal necrosis.

name: Progressive outer retinal necrosis
definition: Fulminant varicella-zoster retinitis in severely immunocompromised (AIDS) patients with multifocal deep outer retinal opacification that rapidly coalesces, with little vitritis.

location.notes: Multifocal, posterior pole and periphery, rapidly confluent to total retinal necrosis.

typical_size: Small foci coalescing to large areas

drawing.description: Draw multiple deep yellow patches across the fundus, merging where confluent; do not add vitreous haze unless present.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (YELLOW = retinal inflammation)

pubmed.title: The progressive outer retinal necrosis syndrome.

name: Candida (fungal) chorioretinitis
definition: Endogenous fungal infection producing multifocal fluffy white chorioretinal lesions that may extend into the vitreous as cotton-ball opacities.

location.notes: Multifocal posterior pole and midperiphery, often bilateral, with overlying vitreous puffballs.

typical_size: About 0.25-1 DD each

drawing.description: Draw creamy yellow fluffy chorioretinal foci and overlying green vitreous puffballs.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (YELLOW = retinal inflammation); green vitreous opacities per CMS L33567 App A

pubmed.title: Endogenous Endophthalmitis - A Major Review.
LASER PHOTOCOAGULATION TREATMENT FOR CANDIDA CHORIORETINITIS.

name: Endophthalmitis vitreous opacity / vitritis
definition: Diffuse inflammatory/infectious opacification of the vitreous (vitritis, vitreous abscess) obscuring fundus detail, the hallmark of endophthalmitis.

location.notes: Diffuse or localised over an infective focus; often densest inferiorly.

typical_size: Localised to the whole vitreous cavity

drawing.description: Shade the obscured area with green stippling, denser where the haze is denser.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

pubmed.title: Gram-Negative Endogenous Endophthalmitis: A Systematic Review.
Endogenous Endophthalmitis - A Major Review.

name: Chorioretinal scar
definition: Healed focal chorioretinal lesion of inflammatory, infectious or traumatic origin, seen as a well-demarcated atrophic area exposing sclera or choroidal vessels with variable pigmented margins.

location.notes: Anywhere; record number and position.

typical_size: Pinpoint to several DD

drawing.description: Outline the scar in black, leave the atrophic centre white, and stipple black where it is pigmented.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (BLACK = scar, pigment clumping); white bare-sclera centre inferred

name: Histo spots (presumed ocular histoplasmosis)
definition: Small discrete punched-out atrophic chorioretinal scars in the macula and midperiphery, with peripapillary atrophy and no vitritis, forming with choroidal neovascularisation the classic triad of presumed ocular histoplasmosis syndrome.

location.notes: Macula and midperiphery plus peripapillary atrophy; occasionally in linear peripheral streaks.

typical_size: Small spots, roughly 0.2-0.7 DD each

drawing.description: Draw scattered small white spots with black pigmented rims, plus peripapillary atrophy; mark any CNV with the CMS neovascularisation colours.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (BLACK = scar); white atrophic centre inferred

pubmed.title: Presumed ocular histoplasmosis syndrome: update on epidemiology, pathogenesis, and photodynamic, antiangiogenic, and surgical therapies.
New and classic insights into presumed ocular histoplasmosis syndrome and its treatment.

name: Multifocal choroiditis (with panuveitis)
definition: Idiopathic inflammatory chorioretinopathy with multiple yellow-grey choroidal spots in the posterior pole and periphery plus vitritis, evolving into punched-out pigmented chorioretinal scars, sometimes with CNV or subretinal fibrosis.

location.notes: Posterior pole, peripapillary and peripheral; may be clustered or linear.

typical_size: About 0.1-0.5 DD per spot

drawing.description: Draw active spots as small yellow dots; redraw inactive spots as white spots with black rims (chorioretinal scar code).

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (YELLOW = inflammation; BLACK = scar)

Multifocal choroiditis with panuveitis and punctate inner choroidopathy: a mini review.

name: Punctate inner choroidopathy
definition: Idiopathic multifocal chorioretinopathy of young myopic women with small yellow-white punctate lesions of the inner choroid/outer retina in the posterior pole, without significant vitritis, often complicated by CNV.

location.notes: Macula and posterior pole.

typical_size: Small punctate lesions, under about 0.25 DD

drawing.description: Draw small yellow dots in the posterior pole; inactive lesions as tiny black-rimmed atrophic scars; CNV with the CMS neovascularisation colours.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (YELLOW = inflammation)

pubmed.title: Punctate inner choroidopathy: A review.
Punctate inner choroidopathy: A review of the current diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.

name: Birdshot chorioretinopathy lesions
definition: Bilateral chronic HLA-A29-associated posterior uveitis with multiple cream-coloured, ovoid hypopigmented choroidal spots radiating from the disc, with vitritis.

location.typical_clock: nasal and inferior to the disc
location.notes: Postequatorial, radiating outward from the disc, concentrated nasally/inferiorly; bilateral.

typical_size: About 1/4-1/2 DD per spot

drawing.description: Draw many small cream-yellow ovals radiating from the disc, densest nasally and inferiorly, with green vitreous haze if active.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (YELLOW = inflammation, atrophic areas)

pubmed.title: Birdshot chorioretinopathy.
Birdshot Chorioretinopathy: A Review.

name: Serpiginous choroiditis
definition: Chronic recurrent inflammation of the choroid, choriocapillaris and RPE spreading in a serpentine/geographic pattern, classically from the peripapillary region, with grey-yellow active edges and atrophic pigmented scars.

location.notes: Peripapillary (classic), macular or ampiginous types; tubercular serpiginous-like lesions may begin multifocally in the periphery.

typical_size: From 1 DD to large geographic areas

drawing.description: Draw the atrophic geographic area white with black pigment stippling extending in pseudopods from the disc; mark active advancing edges with a yellow outline.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (YELLOW = inflammation; BLACK = scar)

pubmed.title: Serpiginous choroiditis.
Tubercular serpiginous choroiditis.

name: APMPPE placoid lesions
synonyms: a p m p p e
acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy
definition: Acute inflammatory choriocapillaritis producing multiple flat, cream-coloured placoid lesions at the level of the outer retina/RPE in the posterior pole, healing with RPE mottling.

location.notes: Posterior pole, usually bilateral.

typical_size: About 1/2-1 DD per plaque

drawing.description: Draw multiple flat creamy yellow plaques in the posterior pole; redraw healed lesions as brown/black mottling.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (YELLOW = inflammation)

pubmed.title: Acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy (APMPPE).

name: MEWDS white dots
definition: Usually unilateral, self-limited choriocapillaritis with subtle small white-grey dots at the outer retinal level in the posterior pole and midperiphery and a granular fovea.

location.notes: Posterior pole and midperiphery around the disc and arcades; fovea granular.

typical_size: Tiny dots, under about 1/4 DD

drawing.description: Draw tiny faint yellow dots around the posterior pole and lightly stipple the fovea for granularity.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (YELLOW = inflammation)

pubmed.title: Multiple evanescent white dot syndrome (MEWDS): update on practical appraisal, diagnosis and clinicopathology; a review and an alternative comprehensive perspective.

name: Acute syphilitic posterior placoid chorioretinitis
definition: Characteristic ocular syphilis lesion: a large, yellowish placoid lesion at the level of the outer retina/RPE in the macula or juxtapapillary region, often with vitritis and punctate preretinal precipitates.

location.notes: Macula or juxtapapillary posterior pole; uni- or bilateral.

typical_size: Large, typically more than 1 DD

drawing.description: Draw a large round yellow placoid patch over the macula; add green vitreous haze/preretinal precipitates if present.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (YELLOW = inflammation)

pubmed.title: Acute syphilitic posterior placoid chorioretinitis: when the great mimicker cannot pretend any more; new insight of an old acquaintance.

name: Choroidal tubercles / tuberculoma (choroidal granuloma)
definition: Yellow-white elevated choroidal inflammatory mass (tuberculoma) or multiple small yellow choroidal tubercles from Mycobacterium tuberculosis (also seen in sarcoidosis), sometimes with overlying exudative detachment.

location.notes: Posterior pole and midperiphery; tubercles multiple, tuberculoma usually solitary.

typical_size: Tubercles about 0.25-1 DD; tuberculoma several DD

drawing.description: Draw a yellow nodule with a brown outline for a choroidal mass; draw miliary tubercles as multiple small yellow dots; exudative detachment in blue.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (YELLOW = inflammation, amelanotic mass); brown outline = choroidal lesion (https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology)

name: Toxocara posterior pole granuloma
definition: Ocular toxocariasis presenting as a white or yellowish elevated inflammatory granuloma in the posterior pole, often with epiretinal membrane, traction bands or retinal folds.

location.notes: Posterior pole/macula, usually unilateral, in children and young adults.

typical_size: About 0.5-2 DD

drawing.description: Draw a white-yellow elevated nodule filled yellow; draw traction bands or epiretinal membrane in green.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (YELLOW = inflammation; GREEN = preretinal fibrosis/membranes)

name: Toxocara peripheral granuloma with traction band
definition: Peripheral form of ocular toxocariasis: a white granuloma in the peripheral retina with a fibrous vitreous band or retinal fold running toward the optic disc, which may drag the macula.

location.notes: Any quadrant near the ora; the band or fold runs from the granuloma to the disc.

typical_size: Granuloma about 1-2 DD plus a band crossing the fundus

drawing.description: Draw a yellow peripheral nodule at or near the ora and a green band (fibrous traction or fold) running from it to the disc.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (YELLOW = inflammation; GREEN = preretinal fibrosis/membranes)

name: Pars planitis snowbank
definition: Grey-white fibroglial inflammatory exudate over the inferior pars plana and vitreous base in pars planitis (idiopathic intermediate uveitis).

location.notes: Drawn in the band between the ora serrata and ciliary-process circles; may be accompanied by peripheral vasculitis.

typical_size: About 2-6 clock hours inferiorly

drawing.description: Shade a stippled green band over the inferior pars plana between the ora and ciliary-process circles.

color_source: inferred: preretinal/vitreous-base opacity drawn green (CMS L33567 App A 'opacities in media'; Jayanna S, Shanmugam PM. Indian J Ophthalmol 2022, https://doi.org/10.4103/ijo.IJO_1004_22)

name: Vitreous snowballs
definition: Discrete white-grey inflammatory cell aggregates in the inferior vitreous, typical of intermediate uveitis (pars planitis, sarcoidosis) and also seen in fungal infection.

location.notes: Inferior peripheral vitreous, near the vitreous base.

typical_size: Small, under about 1/4 DD each

drawing.description: Draw small green circles over the inferior periphery to show vitreous snowballs.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A

name: Retinal vasculitis / perivascular sheathing
definition: Inflammation of retinal vessels, veins more than arteries, seen as white perivascular sheathing or cuffing, sometimes with vascular occlusion and haemorrhage.

location.notes: Peripheral or posterior vessel segments; often with intermediate or posterior uveitis.

typical_size: One vessel segment to multiple vessels

drawing.description: Flank the involved vessel segment with parallel black lines to show sheathing; add red haemorrhages and mark occluded segments in brown per CMS.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology, https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (BLACK = sheathed vessels)

name: Dalen-Fuchs nodules
definition: Small yellow-white nodules between Bruch membrane and the RPE in the midperipheral fundus, characteristic of sympathetic ophthalmia (also seen in Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease).

location.notes: Scattered in the midperiphery of both eyes.

typical_size: Small, about 1/8-1/4 DD each

drawing.description: Draw scattered small yellow dots in the midperiphery of both eyes.

color_source: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (YELLOW = inflammation)
